claims.hypothesis: Does ALMA 12m-alone filtering corrupt core and filament properties before the MRS is reached?
claims.experiment: Noise-free CASA simulations of Gaussian cores and filaments of increasing FWHM, measuring recovered flux, peak and FWHM with 12m alone
claims.result: Large flux losses and FWHM underestimation already appear at sizes below the MRS (12m alone ~20% flux recovery at MRS for cores, ~95% loss for filaments)
claims.finding: 12m-alone data systematically bias derived physical properties well before the MRS

evidence.quote: well before the maximum recoverable scale of the interferometer.

claims.hypothesis: Does adding the ACA 7m array solve the short-spacing problem?
claims.experiment: Compare 12m alone with 12m+7m in cores, filaments and PSF analysis
claims.result: 12m+7m recovers more flux but still loses emission above ~30 arcsec and adds a ~7% PSF sidelobe
claims.finding: 7m improves recovery only partially and degrades the PSF

evidence.quote: These effects are only partially mitigated by the addition of the ALMA ACA-7m array

claims.hypothesis: Does adding Total Power data recover the true sky emission?
claims.experiment: Feather and MACF combinations of 12m+7m with simulated TP
claims.result: Flux recovery >=80% for cores and ~100% for Gaussian filaments; MACF slightly better than Feather within 10%
claims.finding: Total Power is needed to recover emission down to a few beam sizes with <10% error

evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that only the addition of the ALMA Total Power information allows to recover the true sky emission down to few times the ALMA beamsize with satisfactory accuracy

claims.hypothesis: Is a large single dish such as the IRAM-30m better than ACA-7m+TP, and must its sensitivity match the interferometer?
claims.experiment: Combine 12m with a simulated 25 arcsec SD using MACF and raise SD noise to 1, 5 and 10 times the prediction
claims.result: 12m+IRAM-30m MACF is the best method (within ~10% of the model) and tolerates SD noise up to ~5x
claims.finding: A large SD gives better recovery and the sensitivity match can be relaxed

evidence.loc: Data combination with a large SD
evidence.quote: In agreement to our predictions, the ALMA 12m + IRAM-30m MACF appears as the best data combination method.

evidence.loc: On the SD sensitivity for data combination
evidence.quote: a moderate increase of the SD noise level (up to 5 times) does not affect the recovery of the extended emission unless the SD image is heavily corrupted

claims.hypothesis: Do the simulated biases appear in real ALMA data?
claims.experiment: Compare 12m alone and 12m+IRAM-30m Feather and MACF radial profiles of 23 OMC-3 fibers with simulated trends
claims.result: 12m-alone fibers depart from the reference following the simulated trends with a scatter of a factor ~2
claims.finding: Real OMC-3 data confirm the filtering effects

evidence.quote: These new observational results are in close agreement with those in our simulations.

claims.hypothesis: Can interferometric filtering bias the observed core mass function?
claims.experiment: Simulate 500 cores with a Salpeter-like CMF and recover masses with 12m alone and MACF
claims.result: 12m alone gives a shallower CMF (alpha = -1.18) shifted to low masses; MACF reproduces the input slope
claims.finding: Filtering can produce an apparent top-heavy CMF

referee_caveats_inferred: Single noise-free realisation per model; no uncertainties are given on recovery fractions
Only 100 GHz, one field position and C43-1, so conclusions at other bands and configurations are untested
Real-data comparison uses the 12m+IRAM-30m MACF map as truth, which is itself not an independent ground truth
TP is simulated by Gaussian smoothing only, not by a realistic scanning observation, so TP-specific systematics may be missing
